newsitem.title: USA: Chino copper workers to continue seeking pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Chino copper workers to continue seeking pay hike.

text.p: A union leader at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine in New Mexico said workers would still seek a pay hike when stalled labor talks resume Thursday and Friday, despite the company's insistence on a pay freeze.

"Let us not forget that pay at Chino is significantly lower than the rest of the industry right now, so they have some catch-up to do besides some money," United Steelworker of America Chino lead negotiator Robert Guadiana said.
ASARCO and Kennecott Utah Copper workers won a hike of $2.60 per hour over six year, Guadiana said.
Phelps Dodge officials were not immediately available for comment.
Phelps and the USWA will hold their first meeting Thursday at 1300 local time in Las Cruces, New Mexico.
On April 10 Phelp's Treasurer Tom Foster reiterated that pay freeze offer presented last August was still the final deal on the table.
Chino workers have been without a labor contract since June 30 last year.
Guadiana said the USWA had launched a corporate campaign against Phelps Dodge.
"It's getting very, very ugly," Guadiana said. "I am just concerned about escalated activity by the workers and by Phelps Dodge."
Chino is still operating normally at present, Guadiana added.
The mine produces some 160,000 short tons of contained copper in concentrates a year along with some cathode.
